result.title: Evidence for contact delocalization in atomic scale friction

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text analyzes a two-spring model to explain fine structure in atomic stick-slip motion during Friction Force Microscopy. It demonstrates that tip apex delocalization occurs when the effective tip mass is sufficiently low, causing rapid thermally activated motion. This behavior contrasts with the traditional single-spring model and provides insights into macroscopic friction origins.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text analyzes a two-mass-two-spring system where an ultra-low tip mass leads to contact delocalization and complex slip dynamics. A hybrid Langevin-Monte-Carlo scheme reveals that rapid tip motion is not averaged out by the cantilever, creating distinct observable regimes. These findings explain the 'fine structure' of slip events observed in high-resolution experiments, contradicting the 'multiple nanotips' hypothesis.

It establishes a hierarchy of frequencies and uses a Langevin-Monte-Carlo scheme to model cantilever motion and thermally activated tip jumps. The model assumes a sinusoidal tip-surface interaction and neglects direct cantilever damping.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study uses a two-mass-two-spring model with specific parameters to simulate atomic-scale friction, including a tip mass of 10^-20 kg and a cantilever mass of 5.5*10^-11 kg. It identifies distinct slip regimes based on surface corrugation, ranging from trivial slips at high corrugation to smoothened stochastic behavior at low corrugation. The model reveals that at intermediate corrugations, the tip apex experiences a double-well potential, leading to complex slip dynamics.

knowledge_units.context_summary: In the two-well regime, the tip apex delocalizes due to rapid thermal jumps, causing the cantilever to experience an effective potential based on the mean apex position. This effective potential is flattened and the mean force is reduced because rapid oscillations of the instantaneous force average out. The transition from one to two potential states occurs smoothly over a period of time that is related to the jump rate and influences the observed sliding dynamics.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study identifies that single-slip behavior occurs at both high and very low surface corrugations due to the narrowness of the two-well interval. Comparison with experimental data confirms the predicted fine structure and lateral force ranges, though experimental slip durations are longer, suggesting non-sinusoidal surface potentials. Simulations indicate the effective tip mass is less than 10^-18 kg, as larger masses suppress the intermediate states characteristic of contact delocalization.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text describes how contact delocalization can occur at any cantilever position, necessitating a reconsideration of lateral force amplitude, slip times, and thermal noise in FFM measurements. It identifies rapid tip apex motion in the GHz range as the key element for energy dissipation, which occurs via intratip vibration damping or apex-substrate motion damping. The findings suggest that thermally driven dynamics from local surface compliance may influence macroscopic sliding friction.
